articles.title: Bilevel Optimisation: Why Meta-Learning Is an Optimisation Problem Inside an Optimisation Problem
articles.excerpt: Most optimisation problems have one level: pick parameters, minimise a loss, stop. Bilevel optimisation has two. An outer problem chooses some variables, and an inner problem then optimises the rest,…
articles.body: Most optimisation problems have one level: pick parameters, minimise a loss, stop. Bilevel optimisation has two. An outer problem chooses some variables, and an inner problem then optimises the rest, conditional on that choice. The outer objective can only be evaluated after the inner problem has been solved, at least approximately. That nesting shows up far more often than the name suggests. Hyperparameter tuning is bilevel: the outer variables are hyperparameters, the inner variables are model weights trained with those hyperparameters. Meta-learning is bilevel: the outer variables are a shared initialisation or learning rule, and the inner problem is fast adaptation to a new task. Data reweighting, architecture search, and some approaches to cleaning noisy labels are bilevel too.

articles.title: The “Broken Handshake” Liability: Why Agency Agreements Must Define Post-Termination Asset Custody
articles.excerpt: When an agency retainer ends, the digital relationship often doesn’t. Long after the final invoice is paid, the agency may still be logged in, listed as an account owner or admin, or connected through…
articles.body: When an agency retainer ends, the digital relationship often doesn’t. Long after the final invoice is paid, the agency may still be logged in, listed as an account owner or admin, or connected through live API keys and OAuth tokens to its former client’s systems. This article calls that leftover access orphaned administrative authority , and uses “Broken Handshake” as shorthand for the moment the commercial relationship ends but the technical one does not. Neither term is a legal standard. The assets involved include domain registrars, cloud infrastructure (AWS, Google Cloud), ad platforms (Meta, Google Ads, TikTok), analytics and tag management, and SaaS and martech integrations. When the agreement says nothing about who holds these assets after exit, small lapses can cause real damage.

articles.title: Choosing Email APIs for Evidence-Ready Password Resets in B2B SaaS
articles.excerpt: Short answer: choose the email API that leaves a clear trail for every password-reset decision, not the one with the longest template feature list. For a B2B SaaS product, I would separate template re…
articles.body: Short answer: choose the email API that leaves a clear trail for every password-reset decision, not the one with the longest template feature list. For a B2B SaaS product, I would separate template rendering, recipient safety, attachment handling, and delivery evidence. Infrai is a reasonable fit when one REST API, one key, and one bill across backend services reduce operational sprawl, but Amazon SES, SendGrid, and Postmark remain credible choices when their surrounding tooling matches your compliance process. The useful boundary is simple: create one reviewed reset template, render it with a short-lived token, send it once, and retain the request ID plus the template version in your application evidence store.

articles.title: Kubernetes Networking & Ingress Basics (2026): Pods, Services, DNS and Getting Traffic In
articles.excerpt: TL;DR The model in one line: every pod gets a real IP and can talk to every other pod; Services give those shifting pods a stable address; Ingress (or Gateway API) is the front door for HTTP from outs…
articles.body: TL;DR The model in one line: every pod gets a real IP and can talk to every other pod; Services give those shifting pods a stable address; Ingress (or Gateway API) is the front door for HTTP from outside. A Service doesn't contain pods — it points at them, via label selectors, and the live list of targets is the EndpointSlice. "Service exists but nothing answers" almost always means the selector and the pod labels disagree. Cluster DNS is the phone book: service.namespace.svc.cluster.local , resolved by CoreDNS. Most "the app can't reach the database" bugs are DNS or selector bugs wearing a network costume. Ingress is just rules; an Ingress controller is the thing that enforces them. An Ingress object with no controller installed does exactly nothing, silently.

The malicious version, 2.1.313, subsequently affected “at most 5,000 users,” presumably when they either downloaded it or their systems automatically fetched and installed it. A GSLV Mark II rocket launched the nation's NVS-03 satellite from Satish Dhawan Space Centre today at 2:21 p.m. EDT (1821 GMT and 11:51 p.m. India Standard Time). Everything went well: The rocket deployed NVS-03 into geostationary transfer orbit as planned, officials with the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) announced on X about 30 minutes after liftoff. An Indian GSLV Mark II rocket launches the NVS-03 navigation satellite on Oct. 30, 2026. (Image credit: ISRO) NVS-03 is the third next-gen satellite that India has launched for the Navigation with Indian Constellation (NavIC), its version of the United States' Global Positioning System ( GPS ).

articles.title: 5 horror franchises that went to space... and one that absolutely should have but didn't
articles.excerpt: In space, no one can hear you scream, a bit like the empty theater screens that some horror franchise's final installments limp. But there are still some real gems among the space-based frightfests.
articles.body: In space, no one can hear you scream... not unlike in the empty theater screens that aging horror franchises play to when the lustre has gone and their final installments limp to the public. It is perhaps little wonder that some horror franchises go to space to die... or take long breaks, at least. In celebration of Halloween , we're running down some horror franchises that made the journey to the final frontier, resulting in films that range from the sublime and outrageously campy fun to just pure awful. Absent from the list are space horror movies that have space baked into their natural fabric. So no Event Horizon, no Alien, and no Critters 4 (they were aliens, so they just went back to space; that doesn't count). 1.
